text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
The man known as the "Grey Forefather of Australian Poets", CHARLES HARPUR, was born on this day in 1813.
Australian shoe magnate THOMAS FISHER was born in 1820. He left his money to found the Fisher Library at Sydney University because he lived nearby and liked to stroll around the grounds.
French impressionist painter EDOUARD MANET was born in 1832.

Australian architect JOHN CLARK (also known as James), whose works included Government House in Melbourne, the Melbourne Treasury, Newcastle Hospital and the Masonic Hall in Brisbane, was born in 1838.
Australian international tennis star ADRIAN QUIST was born in 1913.
British football player, trainer and Liverpool Manager BOB PAISLEY was born in 1919.
Actress and singing star of Broadway musicals CHITA RIVERA was born in 1933.
British fashion designer whose influence was felt in the 1960s and 70s, BILL GIBB, was born on this day in 1943.

One of the POINTER sisters ANITA was born on this day in 1948. The group made its first records in 1971 and in 1976 they appeared in the film "Car Wash". HIts included "Fire"(1978), "Here's So Shy" (1980), "Slow Hand" (1981), "Jump For My Love" (1984) and "Neutron Dance" (1984).

US singer/songwriter with the 'Doobie Brothers' PAT SIMMONS was born in 1950. The group formed in 1970. Doobie is the Californian slang term for a marijuana joint. Their first records appeared in April 1971. They broke up in 1983 and SIMMONS undertook a brief solo career. His greatest hit was "So Wrong" in 1983. The group reformed in 1989. Their greatest hits included "Long Train Runnin'" (1974), "Black Water" (1974), "What A Fool Believes" (1979), "Real Love" (1980) and "The Doctor" (1989).
** EVENTS **
1556 : More than 830,000 people died in an earthquake in
SHANXI PROVINCE in China.
1806 : England's youngest Prime Minister, WILLIAM PITT
the Younger, died at the age of 47. He first took Office at the age of 24.
1849 : British born ELIZABETH BLACKWELL qualified as the
first woman doctor in the United States.
1900 : In the second British-Boer War, the British
attempt to break through the Boer lines to relieve Ladysmith was thwarted at the Battle of Spion Kop.
1909 : The new 7,000 mile telegraphic link between London
and India was hailed as a great achievement.
1928 : An earthquake rocked Nazareth near Jerusalem.
1931 : ANNA PAVLOVA, the Russian prima ballerina, died at
the age of 45.
1943 : In World War Two, the British under Field Marshal
MONTGOMERY captured Tripoli, Libya.
1946 : At the Nuremberg War crimes trials top Nazi

RUDOLPH HESS asked to conduct his own defence. He was HITLER's private secretary and deputy. In May 1941 he landed in Britain with peace proposals and was held prisoner until 1945. He was convicted of war crimes and sentenced to life imprisonment. He died in Berlin's Spandau prison in 1987.
1963 : HAROLD "KIM" PHILBY, British journalist in Beirut,
disappeared. Later in the year it was revealed that he was the third man in the BURGESS-MACLEAN espionage affair and had been granted asylum in Moscow.
1970 : London's Heathrow airport saw its first giant jet

airliner, known as the "Jumbo". The Pan Am jet carried twice as many passengers as the Boeing 707. The airport's facilities had difficulty coping with the increased numbers and lots of luggage went astray. The plane arrived three hours late because of engine trouble and one engine had to be changed before it took off from New York, its next leg of the inaugural flight had to be cancelled because of bad weather.
1973 : President RICHARD NIXON told the American public
that the war in Vietnam had ended, with a peace treaty expected to be signed within days.
1976 : PAUL ROBESON, the black American singer, actor and
campaigner for civil rights, died at the age of 77.
1978 : Sweden became the first country to ban the use of
aerosol cans.
1989 : Spanish surrealist painter SALVADOR DALI, died at
1989 : The Soviet Union suffered a human tragedy with the

death of more than one thousand people killed by a dawn earthquake in the Central Asian republic of Tajikistan. The earthquake, which measured 5.5 on the Richter Scale, had its epicentre near two villages which were swallowed in landslides.
1995 : JACQUES DELORS formally stepped down as European
Commission president, handing over to JACQUES SANTER after 10 years of steering Europe towards closer union.
